plancap

plancap estimates the floorspace and dwellings that planning rules enable on each land parcel, for any jurisdiction, and summarises, compares and plots the result.

Planning rules (height limits, setbacks, recession or daylight planes, site coverage, landscaping, floor area ratios, density controls, overlays and precincts) are entered as a rulebook: a validated set of rules with a citation for every value, written in R, as a YAML file, or in an Excel template. Capacity is built site by site as a stack of storey footprints clipped by every rule that applies, then summarised by zone, height, location or the rule that binds. Plan changes are compared as scenarios, with the change split into what drove it.

From parcels to results 

library(plancap)
town <- exampleton()

sc <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
               parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
               roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
               zoning = town$zoning, layers = town[c("height_areas", "transit")])
cap <- estimate_capacity(sc)

summary(cap)                          # headline, by zone, what limits dwellings
check_capacity(cap)                   # reconciliation: parcels, land, storeys
summarise_capacity(cap, by = c("zone", "height_band"))
plot_capacity(cap)                    # floor area by zone
plot_constraints(cap)                 # from the theoretical maximum to enabled
explain_site(cap, "P00001")           # every setback at every storey, with citations

A plan change is a scenario that states only what differs:

pc1 <- exampleton_pc1()
change <- scenario_change(sc, "PC1", rulebook = pc1$rulebook, zoning = pc1$zoning)
cmp <- compare_scenarios(run_scenarios(scenario_set(sc, change)))
plot_attribution(cmp)                 # rules, zoning, overlays, parcels

What it covers

  • Rules: yards, recession and daylight planes (graded by orientation, turning vertical, measured from the far side of a road), upper-level and height-proportional setbacks, any setback profile, alternative standards, coverage, landscaping, impervious area, floor area ratio, floorplate and tower limits, building length and separation, the site shape factor, density, access width, height overlays and surfaces, exclusions, precincts with dwelling totals, bonuses and entitlements; any value may be a formula.
  • Sites: road, side and rear boundaries, corner, through and rear sites, access legs and rights of way, the zone across each boundary, water boundaries, sloping ground; every assumption adjustable.
  • Summaries and plots: one summarise_capacity() for every breakdown, a constraint waterfall, sensitivity sweeps, maps, a 3D view, and comparison plots, in one quiet, colour-blind-safe theme.
  • Verified: it reproduces the capacityengine model exactly on an Auckland tile, including the effect of Plan Change 120.

Rulebooks that ship 

rulebook_examples()
#> "auckland" "christchurch" "exampleton" "exampleton_pc1" "hamilton" "wellington"

Exampleton and its plan change are fictional. Auckland, Christchurch, Wellington and Hamilton are dated worked examples: check the plan before relying on any value. The vignette Adding a new jurisdiction: Hamilton enters a real plan through the Excel template, from the plan text to results.

Scope

plancap estimates plan-enabled, gross, blank-slate capacity: what the rules would allow on each site if no buildings existed. It does not estimate feasible, infrastructure-ready or likely development. See Method and assumptions.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("faceteconomics/plancap")
